result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of narrow sidewalks on both sides of a residential street, significantly obstructed by utility poles. There are no visible marked crossings, lane markings, or traffic calming measures, which limits pedestrian safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Utility poles on sidewalk
hazards.description: Utility poles are placed directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk, creating a physical barrier for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids or strollers.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks visible, which fails to designate a safe space for pedestrians to cross the roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-style crosswalks at the nearest intersection to improve pedestrian visibility and right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at intersections to reduce crossing distance and prevent cars from parking too close to the corner, improving sightlines.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add center and edge line markings to the roadway to better organize vehicle traffic and potentially reduce speeds.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk adjacent to a fenced park and parking area. While the walkway is clear and continuous, there is no physical buffer between pedestrians and the roadway, and no crossing infrastructure is visible in this midblock section.

hazards.name: Sun Glare
hazards.description: Intense direct sunlight and glare can significantly reduce driver visibility of pedestrians on the sidewalk or road.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the sidewalk and the active travel lane.

hazards.name: Roadway Debris
hazards.description: Large pieces of cardboard or similar debris are present in the roadway, which could cause vehicle swerving.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strip
interventions.description: Install a landscaped buffer between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: If a crossing is needed, curb extensions would reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The street provides basic pedestrian infrastructure with sidewalks on both sides, but lacks any formal crossing treatments or traffic calming measures. The environment is characterized by a mix of residential row houses and a large fenced parking lot, which creates a significant stretch of blank frontage and reduced natural surveillance.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Trash bags and debris are placed on the left sidewalk, narrowing the effective walking width.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross the unmarked roadway without designated priority.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The long chain-link fence on the left side creates a lack of natural surveillance and a less comfortable pedestrian environment.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Introduce street trees and a buffer zone to separate the sidewalk from moving traffic and improve the walking environment.

result.summary: The image shows a typical residential mid-block environment with continuous concrete sidewalks and row house frontage. While the walkway is clear and in good condition, there is a lack of pedestrian amenities such as street trees, lighting, or a buffer from the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the sidewalk and the roadway, placing pedestrians in close proximity to moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground

hazards.name: Absence of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No street light poles are visible in the immediate vicinity, which may create safety concerns for pedestrians after dark.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Install street trees or a furniture zone to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the street.
